transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Mostly it’s my sleep. It’s gotten completely out of control. At first I’d sleep maybe two or three hours and then be up, drafting plans, feeling like I was ready to get going. Now I’m lying awake before dawn with my stomach tight, and I don’t feel rested at all.
Have you been feeling unusually energetic or active recently?

Yes. I felt like I had an engine running inside me. Sitting still was almost impossible, so I’d be up before sunrise calling people, rewriting proposals, jumping from one thing to the next without really stopping.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?
I’m not really sure I’d call it sad. I haven’t noticed feeling especially down, no. It’s more that I feel worn out and unsettled.
Have you been feeling anxious?
I don’t really know. I’ve felt keyed up and unsettled, but I’m not sure I’d call it anxiety exactly.
Have you been feeling hopeless about your future?

Yes… I guess I have. I keep going over that investment decision in my head, telling myself I’ve ruined my wife’s security. Like I made a fool of myself after a whole lifetime of trying to be the responsible one.
Have you ever had a period where you felt extremely high or euphoric?

Yes. For a few weeks I felt almost… unusually optimistic, like everything was going to work out and any problem was easy to get past. But I was also quick to get angry if someone questioned me. I’d snap at them, like they were the ones being unreasonable.
Have you lost interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yes. I used to spend whole afternoons at the museum, or get absorbed in photography or cooking. Lately I’ll look at my camera, or even think about sitting down to play bridge, and I just feel… nothing. Mostly it just feels like it would take effort to pretend I’m enjoying it.
How long did this extremely optimistic feeling last?

It lasted for weeks. I don’t remember the exact number, but it wasn’t just a day or two — I felt almost brilliantly optimistic for quite a while, like every problem was small. And during that same stretch, if anyone questioned me, I’d snap at them.
Did you ever feel so good or hyper that you got into trouble for being too outgoing or reckless?

Yes, I suppose so. I became much more… active than usual. I started mentoring several companies at once, writing up fundraising ideas, setting up lunches with half the town. In retirement, that’s way more than I’d normally take on.
Did you notice your extremely optimistic feelings switching back and forth with periods where you felt really down?

Yes, it did feel like it went back and forth. For weeks I’d feel almost brilliantly optimistic, like every obstacle was nothing, and then I’d hit stretches where I felt really down. During that high period, if anyone questioned me, I’d snap at them, like they were getting in the way or trying to undermine me.
Have you had a period of at least two weeks where you felt sad or empty most of the day?
Yes. It’s been much longer than two weeks. Since those plans fell apart, I’ve been feeling low and guilty and mostly withdrawn… about nine months now.
Did your periods of feeling extremely optimistic and your periods of feeling really down tend to happen one after the other?
I’m not really sure. I can tell they were different periods, but I don’t know if they always came right one after the other in a clear pattern. It’s a bit hard for me to line it up exactly.
Did you notice that after feeling really down, you would then feel extremely optimistic again, in a kind of cycle?

Yes, I think that did happen. After being really down, there were times when I’d swing back into feeling almost brilliantly optimistic for weeks, like nothing could really stop me. But I’d also get very irritable if anyone questioned me, like they were trying to get in my way.
Did your periods of feeling extremely optimistic and your periods of feeling really down happen in a regular pattern?
I can’t say it was regular, no. I noticed the ups and downs, but I don’t think they followed a clear schedule or pattern that I could predict.
Did your periods of feeling extremely optimistic and your periods of feeling really down both occur within the past year?
Yes, within the past year. After the investment loss, for about five months I really wasn’t living like my normal retired self. Everything was kind of centered on trying to undo what happened.
Did your periods of feeling extremely optimistic usually last about the same amount of time?

Not really about the same each time, no. The main stretch I remember clearly was after the investment loss — for about five months I wasn’t living like my usual retired self, and everything was focused on trying to undo the damage.
Did both your extremely optimistic periods and your really down periods happen within the same year, without following any predictable pattern?

Yes, both were in that same year, but not in any kind of pattern I could predict. The clearest part was after the investment loss—about five months where I really wasn’t living like my usual retired self. Everything was about trying to undo the damage.
Did your periods of feeling extremely optimistic usually last at least a week?

Yes, the main one definitely lasted more than a week. After that investment loss, it went on for about five months, where I wasn’t really living like my usual retired self and everything was about trying to undo the damage.
Did your periods of feeling extremely optimistic usually last at least two weeks?

Yes. The one I keep thinking of lasted much longer than two weeks — about five months after the investment loss. During that time I just wasn’t living like my normal retired self; everything revolved around trying to fix what had happened.
Did you feel like you returned to a normal mood between your periods of feeling extremely optimistic?
I’m not really sure how to answer that. I don’t remember it as clearly as going back to normal in between. It’s more that things shifted, but I can’t say I noticed a clean return to my usual mood.
